summary: Turn apps/api/src/requests/ from a read-only vacation projection into a real request system, and turn /org/{orgId}/requests from a manager-only vacation feed into everyone's inbox. Three new tables (Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent) plus one defaulted column (Organization.nextRequestNumber) carry a record of somebody needing something from somebody else: type access|question, an addressee, a project, a deadline, a thread and an append-only audit trail. Eight routes are added behind the existing SessionGuard -> OrgScopeGuard chain; five statuses (open, answered, granted, declined, cancelled) move only inside a transaction that re-read the row with FOR UPDATE, and only the requester (or an admin) ever writes granted. The existing vacation aggregation moves unchanged into VacationRequestFeedService and the controller composes two sections into one response, so the page unifies while the model does not. The page-level view-requests gate is deleted and replaced by two inner ones (the vacation section, and the All scope), the sidebar row becomes unconditional, and the badge stops counting the view and starts counting the work. No mail, no job, no new infrastructure, no unauthenticated surface.

tasks.title: Prisma schema + the one additive migration: Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent, Organization.nextRequestNumber

migration.note: One migration for the run. Three new tables and one new column with a default; no rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table, so no backfill. Order read from infra/deploy.sh, not from prose about it: deploy.sh:175-185 registers module.app.aws_ecs_task_definition.migrate and runs infra/migrate.sh as a one-off Fargate task on the NEW image, and only when `api` is among the services being deployed; deploy.sh:187-192 then `tf apply`s the services. The schema therefore changes while the PREVIOUS image is still serving, and the whole safety of that window here is that three unreferenced tables and one defaulted column are invisible to code that does not know about them. Columns exactly as the Data Model states them: Request.assigneeKind String NOT NULL and Request.assigneeMembershipId String NULL (nullable in the column so requests/02's second addressee kind needs no column change; required at the validation layer while assigneeKind = 'member'). FKs: organizationId Cascade, projectId SetNull, requesterMembershipId Cascade, assigneeMembershipId SetNull, resolvedByAccountId SetNull, RequestMessage.requestId and RequestEvent.requestId Cascade, authorMembershipId/actorMembershipId SetNull. Indexes: @@unique([organizationId, number]), @@index([organizationId, status]), @@index([organizationId, assigneeMembershipId, status]), @@index([organizationId, lastActivityAt]), and @@index([requestId, createdAt]) on both child tables. No Prisma enum: every value set is a documented String column, following Project.status (schema.prisma:725) and Client.status (schema.prisma:770), not the documents area's enums. Organization.nextRequestNumber Int @default(1), mirroring Project.nextTaskNumber (schema.prisma:734). Run prisma generate from apps/api, never from the repository root.

buildFromZero: Prisma models Request, RequestMessage and RequestEvent, and the Organization.nextRequestNumber column, in one additive migration.
A write side for apps/api/src/requests/, which is a single read-only aggregation method today.

POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests — validation, 404-not-400 for a cross-org project or membership, number allocation under the organization row lock, and the `created` event in the same transaction.
GET/PATCH /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{requestId} — the party rule, the immutable-field rule, one field_changed event per edited field.
POST .../messages — append-only, 409 in a terminal status, message_posted event, lastActivityAt bump, author display name snapshotted into newLabel.
The four transition routes (answer, grant, decline, cancel) and reassign, each with the FOR UPDATE re-read, the actor guard evaluated against that read, and exactly one RequestEvent.
The decline path that writes its reason as a RequestMessage in the same transaction as the status.
The two-section GET list: scope, four filters, the fixed status mapping onto the spec-10 vacation feed, and the two unfiltered counters.
A strict status/type parser that answers 400 instead of falling back — the opposite of parseRequestStatusFilter's shipped behaviour.
The derived overdue rule, computed per reading account's timezone, with no column and no job.
The default comparator: non-terminal before terminal first, then blocking, then overdue, then priority, then lastActivityAt.
Three capabilities registered in both MemberCapability/CAPABILITY_MATRIX and Capability/ROLE_CAPABILITIES, and the 'party to a request' composition of capability with identity.
31 new REQUEST_MESSAGES keys and the field validators behind them.
The new-request modal, the scope control, the project filter, the free-text search and the two empty states.
The request detail screen: thread, history, action controls, decline reason, reassign, inactive-addressee banner.
The badge rewrite: waitingOnMe plus, for a view-requests holder, the vacation pending count — fetched for every role, from a call that sends no filters.
testIds: requests-card-{id} and every existing requests-card-* id (unchanged, the vacation section keeps them so spec 10's E2E and TC-01-INT-20 stay meaningful)

risks.risk: apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts breaks in three places the spec does not name. Requirement 42 enumerates three callers of the retired vocabulary, but TC-10-INT-03 at :323-340 asserts GET /requests answers 403 with REQUESTS_PAGE_MESSAGES.viewForbidden for user and viewer — which requirement 37 reverses — and the two cases at :342-400 read a top-level requests/pendingCount/totalCount that the new envelope moves under vacation.
risks.mitigation: T9 owns the whole file, not only :301-320. TC-10-INT-03 is retired and its rule replaced by TC-01-INT-18; record the retirement in specs/user-management/10 as `- **Retired.**` naming TC-01-INT-18 and TC-01-E2E-08, because a case deleted without that note is a rule nobody can find again.

risks.risk: packages/validation/src/roles.test.ts asserts exact capability sets. Granting view-own-requests to all four roles makes ROLE_CAPABILITIES.user and .viewer non-empty, breaking capabilitiesFor('member') === [] (:139), capabilitiesFor(null) === [] (:140), the member-equals-user assertion (:184), capabilitiesFor('superadmin') === [] (:188) and capabilitiesFor('self') === [] (:251), as well as the exact admin/manager arrays at :111 and :127.
risks.mitigation: T2 updates all seven assertions in the same commit as the capability additions. The intent of :188 and :251 — an unknown role and a fake 'self' role get nothing beyond what viewer gets — must be preserved by asserting equality with capabilitiesFor('viewer'), not by deleting the cases.

risks.risk: TC-01-E2E-04 needs an overdue row and there is no route to one. Requirement 8 rejects a past neededBy at creation; e2e holds no database handle (no PrismaClient anywhere under e2e/); apps/api/src/test-support/ exposes only envelope expiry and the SignWell stub; and no timezone pair makes tomorrow's date past for a second reader.
risks.mitigation: PATCH is the route, and the spec permits it: requirement 8 scopes the rule to creation ('it may become past afterwards'), and the Error Messages table lists neededByPast under POST alone while every other shared field says POST/PATCH. T5 must therefore NOT re-apply validation rule 6 on PATCH. If a reviewer disagrees, the alternative is a test-support fixture route, which the spec's Verification Plan explicitly claims not to owe — so the disagreement is a spec question, not a code one.

risks.risk: The 400 body for an unknown status or type on GET /requests names no message and no export. TC-01-INT-22 pins the status code only, so two implementations differ in what the page can show.
risks.mitigation: Answer with the shape the same controller family already uses — 400 {"error":"validation_error","fields":{"status":…}} — and invent no new REQUEST_MESSAGES key for it. An unknown value can only arrive from a hand-edited URL, never from the rendered control, so no user-facing copy is needed.

risks.risk: Deleting parseRequestStatusFilter would take a live spec-10 unit suite with it. packages/validation/src/requests-page.test.ts:24-59 pins its fallback behaviour, and requirement 42 retires the vocabulary on this endpoint, not the function.
risks.mitigation: Keep the export and its tests; remove only the two product call sites (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:105 and apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:89,193). The new strict parser is a separate export.

risks.risk: Request creation serializes against unrelated work. The organization row it locks for nextRequestNumber is the same row already locked by member add/remove (members.service.ts:157,379), vacation submit/review/cancel (vacation-requests.service.ts:83,206,340), the vacation service (vacation.service.ts:291) and the accrual run (accrual.service.ts:74).
risks.mitigation: Accepted, and unchanged from the shipped nextTaskNumber pattern: the lock is held for the length of one insert. Keep it that way — no HTTP call, no mail, no PDF work inside the create transaction, and never take the Request row lock while holding the Organization one.

risks.risk: The order in which a transition route checks things decides whether a caller sees 404, 409 or 403, and AC-16 forbids a route answering two ways for one caller.
risks.mitigation: Fix one order in T5 and use it on all five routes: resolve the row scoped by session.organizationId and apply the party rule first (404 for a non-party, identical to a missing row), then the terminal check (409 alreadyTerminal), then the transition legality check (409 invalidTransition), then the actor guard on the locked row (403 notYoursTo*). This is what makes edge case 4a a 403 and TC-01-INT-19 a 404 on every route.

risks.risk: The response envelope changes shape for a route the web app already consumes, and the two consumers read it at different keys.
risks.mitigation: T3, T6 and T8 land together: the page moves from data.requests to data.requests plus data.vacation.requests, and the badge from data.pendingCount to counts.waitingOnMe plus vacation.pendingCount. TC-01-INT-20 pins each vacation row byte-for-byte against the shape e2e/tests/requests-page.spec.ts asserts today, so the envelope may move but a row may not.

risks.risk: The Requests page becomes reachable by every role, and the current page redirects user and viewer to Members at apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:80.
risks.mitigation: T6 removes that redirect. The gate moves inward and nothing else moves with it: the vacation section and the All scope keep view-requests and view-all-requests respectively, so no role sees a pre-existing row it cannot see today — asserted by TC-01-INT-18 and TC-01-E2E-08, with TC-01-E2E-10 as the witness that the nav row did appear.
